**What the Launch Signaled About the Agentic-Coding Market**
The launch signaled that reliability and safety were becoming critical differentiators in an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush. [Source: ev-1]

By highlighting significant advancements in capability, particularly with "computer use 2.0," which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation (referenced here via version comparisons involving 3.x) for browser control tasks [Source: ev-1], Anthropic positioned Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent against competitors like OpenAI's o-series [Source: ev-1].

This strategic focus on reliability and safety drove record API usage and cemented Anthropic’s position in the market, ultimately contributing to its raising of a large funding round at a reported ~$183 billion valuation later that year [Source: ev-1].
Anthropic released Claude 4 as two distinct models, Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

Opus 4 served as the flagship model with higher pricing at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1], while Sonnet 4 acted as a "fast workhorse" positioned specifically as the developer-default coding model at lower prices of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].
